title: The Concept of Cognitive Dissonance
text:
Cognitive dissonance refers to the mental stress or discomfort experienced by an individual who holds two or more contradictory beliefs, ideas, or values, or when their actions conflict with their stated values. This psychological theory posits that humans are motivated toward maintaining internal consistency; therefore, encountering inconsistency creates a compelling need for resolution.

The discomfort of dissonance is powerful because it drives corrective action. To alleviate this tension, individuals typically attempt to change one of the conflicting cognitions, introduce new consonant beliefs, or minimize the importance of the conflict altogether. For instance, smoking while knowing the health risks involves generating justifications that reduce the perceived threat.

This mechanism explains many forms of rationalization observed in human behavior, suggesting that efforts to create a coherent self-narrative often take precedence over seeking objective truth or purely logical outcomes.
